# SK6040 — An `out` variable is declared and never read

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`M(out var x)` where nothing ever mentions `x` again declares a name for a value the code has decided not to look at; `out _` says that.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Design |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 7.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

An `out` argument is a second return value, and a declaration expression is how the caller receives it. When the receiving name is never read, the declaration is doing one thing only — satisfying the signature — and it does that while adding a name to the enclosing scope, a definite-assignment obligation, and a line the next reader has to check before concluding it does not matter. `out _` is the language's word for exactly this: the argument is required, the value is not wanted. It also removes the name from scope, so a later edit cannot accidentally read a value nobody meant to keep, and it makes the two `TryGetValue` calls in a file that differ only in whether the value is used visibly different from each other.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
if (!lookup.TryGetValue(key, out var existing)) {
    lookup.Add(key, value);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
if (!lookup.TryGetValue(key, out _)) {
    lookup.Add(key, value);
}
```

## When it does not fire

**This is one of the nine inspections issue #121 grouped, and it is the only one shipped.** It is the shape with a mechanical, always-safe repair: the callee writes the argument either way, so replacing the declaration with a discard cannot remove a side effect. Removing an unread *ordinary* local cannot promise that — `var response = Send();` is unread and deleting it stops the request — and the remaining seven shapes each need something a single declaration does not carry. `UnusedLocalFunction` is already **CS8321**, a compiler warning, and is not re-implemented here. `NotAccessedVariable`, `UnusedLocalFunctionParameter`, `UnusedTypeParameter` and `UnusedParameterInPartialMethod` have no safe edit; `UnusedLocalFunctionReturnValue` and `UnusedTupleComponentInReturnValue` need every call site. What is left uncovered is named rather than implied, so [17](17-inspection-parity.md)'s residue keeps counting it.

**Only a declaration expression in an `out` argument position.** A pre-declared local (`int n; M(out n);`) is not reported: the declaration is a statement of its own, the repair is to delete it as well as the reference, and that is two edits in two places rather than one replacement. A discard already written is not a declaration and produces nothing.

**Never read *and* never written.** Any reference to the local at all withdraws the finding, including one that only assigns it and one that passes it to a second `out`. That is stricter than "never read" and it is deliberate: `out _` deletes the name, so a finding that only proves the value is unread would produce an edit that does not compile wherever the name is used for anything else.

**A second, redundant guard reads tokens rather than operations.** Before reporting, the enclosing operation blocks are scanned for any identifier token spelling the same name. A match withdraws the finding even when the operation tree showed no reference — the case it is there for is `nameof(x)`, and the cost of being wrong in this direction is one missed finding rather than one broken build. A member or a type with the same name as the variable also silences it; that is the price and it is small.

⚠ **A member containing a preprocessor directive is skipped entirely.** Disabled text is trivia, so a reference inside `#if DEBUG` is invisible to both the operation tree and the token scan, and under another configuration the variable is read. This is the same refusal `SK6003` and `SK6020` make for the same reason.

⚠ **A parameter whose type mentions one of the invoked method's own type parameters is skipped, conservatively.** `out _` is an implicitly typed discard, and CS8183 is what a discard that cannot be typed produces. Whether inference actually fails depends on the rest of the call, and answering that properly means re-running overload resolution; declining is cheaper and only ever costs findings. The related shape the rule cannot see at all is an overload set whose members differ *only* in the `out` parameter's type, where `out _` becomes ambiguous — vanishingly rare, and a compiler error rather than a silent change if it happens.
